summary: Defines a subcode for the BGP Cease NOTIFICATION message to be used when a BGP session is closed because of a BFD session going down. This helps operators see the real reason a connection ended.

eli5.summary: When a phone call is cut off, this adds a label saying the cause was a failed line check, so people know why.

questions: why did my bgp session go down
what is the bgp bfd down subcode
subtitle: A label that tells a BGP neighbor the session was closed because BFD declared the link down.

tldr.problem: When BGP closes a connection because a BFD session went down, the neighbor has no standard way to learn that BFD, and not BGP itself, was the reason.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a new Cease NOTIFICATION subcode, "BFD Down", with value 10, that a BGP speaker SHOULD send when it terminates a connection for this reason.
tldr.outcome: Operators can tell a BFD-detected failure apart from a problem with the BGP speaker. The subcode is purely informational and does not change the BGP state machine.

today: RFC 9384 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why BGP Needs a BFD Reason
sections.content:
BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) detects loss of connectivity between two forwarding engines, typically with low latency. Routing protocols such as BGP use it as an advisory service, so that they can close their connections faster than their own timers would allow.

BGP-4 normally ends a connection when the Hold Timer expires. The minimum Hold Time is at least three seconds, unless KEEPALIVE processing has been disabled by negotiating a Hold Time of zero. When a BFD session goes Down, the BGP speaker sends a Cease NOTIFICATION to the neighbor if possible, then closes the TCP connection. This RFC adds a subcode so the message says why.
sections.eli5: A router can hang up faster if a quick line checker says the line is dead. This gives it a way to tell the other side that the line checker was the reason.

sections.title: The BFD Down Subcode
sections.content:
IANA allocated the value 10 for the BFD Down Cease NOTIFICATION subcode. When a BGP connection is terminated because a BFD session went into the Down state, the speaker SHOULD send a NOTIFICATION with error code Cease and error subcode BFD Down.

The registration is made in the "BGP Cease NOTIFICATION message subcodes" registry, with the name "BFD Down" and a reference to this document.
sections.eli5: It is one new reason code on the list of reasons a router can give when it hangs up. This one means the line check failed.

sections.title: Operational Considerations
sections.content:
BFD can go Down on only a partial loss of connectivity, so the remote speaker may still receive the Cease message. It then knows the connection ended because of a BFD-detected issue and not an issue with the BGP speaker. Operators choose BFD timers by criteria such as stability versus fast failure.

On a total loss of connectivity the message may never be sent. Even so, speakers SHOULD record the reason in their operational state, for example bgpPeerLastError in the BGP MIB or last-error in the BGP YANG model.

When the RFC 8538 procedures for a Cease "Hard Reset" apply and the connection is ending because BFD went Down, the "BFD Down" subcode SHOULD be encapsulated in the Hard Reset's data portion.
sections.eli5: If the line is totally dead, the goodbye note cannot be delivered, so the router writes the reason in its own logbook instead.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Like RFC 4486, this document only adds a subcode that helps operators correlate network events and diagnose peering problems. It is purely informational and has no impact on the BGP Finite State Machine beyond what RFC 4271 already documents in Sections 6.6 and 6.7.
sections.eli5: It is only a note explaining why, so it does not give anyone new powers or change how routers behave.
